source_text: similiter benedicti sint ut Adam et Eva dicente Deo: Crescite et multiplicamini, et replete terram et dominamini eius Voluptas ergo ista, quam tu diabolicam vis videri, iam in supradictis coniugibus habebatur, quae ut institutione bona, ita etiam benedictione permansit. Non enim dubitatur de hac ad Noe et filios eius corporum commixtione dictum, cuius iam usus inoleverat: Crescite et multiplicamini, et replete terram
pass_a_gloss: they were blessed similarly as Adam and Eve, God saying: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth and rule over it. Therefore this pleasure, which you wish to seem diabolical, was already held in the above-said spouses, which as it remained good by institution, so also by blessing. For it is not doubted that this was said of the mixing of bodies to Noah and his sons, whose use had already grown in: Increase and multiply, and fill the earth.
pass_b_english: [Noah and his sons] were blessed in the same way as Adam and Eve, when God said: “Increase and multiply, fill the earth, and rule over it” (Genesis 9:1; Genesis 1:28).

Therefore this pleasure, which you wish to make appear diabolical, was already present in the couples mentioned above. Good in its institution, it also continued under the blessing. There is no doubt that “Increase and multiply and fill the earth” was said to Noah and his sons about the union of bodies whose practice had already become established.

choices.why: Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
rejected: under Satan (name not in the Latin here)

choices.why: Keep Julian's good-of-nature vs good-of-will contrast; do not baptize as 'grace'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, De nuptiis et concupiscentia 2 / On Marriage and Concupiscence); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
kind: Julian excerpt in the intermediary document
